title: Preparing for an Auto Loan
summary: Price → Trade → Fees → APR → Term → Total
subtitle: Audit the whole loan before the payment puts on a tiny disguise

blocks.text: A car payment can look impressively small when the loan has been stretched across several birthdays.

This course teaches you to compare offers by total cost, not by how fast the salesperson talks. You will separate the price from the financing, spot negative equity and add-ons, and read the disclosure. Then you will control credit inquiries and test whether the payment survives insurance, fuel, maintenance and an inconvenient Tuesday.
The payment is one line. The amount financed, the APR, the term and the total payments show what the loan costs in full.

items.title: “The lowest payment is the cheapest offer.”
items.text: A longer term can lower the payment while raising total interest. It can also keep you owing more than the car is worth for longer.

blocks.text: FCAC: Shopping for auto-financing
You can see the full cost of a car loan before the weekly number takes over.
blocks.detail: You will pull price, trade and add-ons apart before financing comes up, so a small weekly payment stays honest.
blocks.extra: Next, the Offer section builds the real price before the payment gets a vote.

sections.title: Build the Price Before Discussing the Payment

blocks.text: If every number is folded into one weekly payment, the paperwork has learned camouflage.

items.title: START WITH CASH PRICE
items.text: Negotiate the vehicle price and write it down before financing comes up. Ask whether any rebate depends on using a certain loan.

items.title: SEPARATE THE TRADE-IN
items.text: Write down the trade value and the exact payout on your old loan. A higher payout creates negative equity that may be added to the new loan.

items.title: LIST FINANCED EXTRAS
items.text: List the taxes, administration fees, registration, warranty, protection, insurance products and every optional add-on.

items.title: READ CREDIT TERMS
items.text: Compare the amount financed, the APR, the payment frequency, the number of payments, the term and the total cost of borrowing.

items.title: ADD OWNERSHIP COSTS
items.text: Get an insurance quote. Estimate fuel or charging, tires, parking, maintenance and repairs.

blocks.text: Negative equity does not vanish when it is rolled in. It becomes old-car debt riding inside the new-car payment.

Gather your ID, proof of income and residence, your current payout, an insurance quote and recent credit reports. Where you can, get quotes from a financial institution and a dealer. Compare them on the same vehicle price, down payment and term.
FCAC says the bureaus treat car-loan or mortgage quotes from different lenders within a two-week period as one inquiry.

items.title: “A dealership must show me its lowest available rate.”
items.text: The offer you are shown may not be the best one available. Compare quotes, and ask which lender, rate, fees, compensation and conditions apply.

blocks.text: FCAC: Car financing options
Meet Lucas
paragraphs: Lucas Martin is a refrigeration technician in Regina who needs a reliable vehicle for early service calls. His hatchback is nearing retirement, with all the dignity of a shopping cart with one stubborn wheel.
A dealer offers a compact SUV for $119 a week. The payment looks comfortable, and the heated seats make a strong Saskatchewan argument.
Then Lucas asks for the worksheet: 84 months, $4,000 of negative equity from his trade-in, paint protection, replacement insurance and an unpriced warranty.

Instead of signing, he takes the quote home and rebuilds it line by line. A bank quote and an insurance estimate show the twist: the weekly payment fits his budget, but the total cost of owning the SUV does not.
Lucas goes back with a price ceiling and a financing ceiling. He removes the extras and refuses to roll the shortfall into a costlier vehicle.

He keeps the hatchback three more months and pays it down, then buys a lower-priced used crossover on a five-year loan. The payment is higher than $119 a week, but the total borrowing cost and the negative-equity risk are both lower.
No one applauds when he signs. The hatchback is finally gone, and the one stubborn wheel went with it.

blocks.text: Lucas controlled the five places where a small payment hides a large debt: price, trade, add-ons, amount financed and term.
What resolved the conflict?
A printed quote, outside financing and a walk-away ceiling turned pressure into a comparison he could finish at home.
You can see what one extra year on a car loan costs.
blocks.detail: You will put an 84-month loan next to a 60-month loan, so about $3,010 in extra interest is a number you saw, not a surprise.

blocks.text: The longer loan buys payment relief, not a discount. If the shorter payment does not fit, a lower vehicle price may be the safer fix.
Before signing

items.title: Read the disclosure statement that shows the total borrowing cost, and keep a copy.
Check the contract price, trade, payout, add-ons, APR, term and payment frequency.
Ask whether optional products can be removed, and how a cancellation or refund affects the loan.
Do not assume you get a next-day cooling-off period. The rules vary by province or territory.
“I can always cancel the vehicle contract tomorrow.”
items.text: There is no national next-day cancellation rule in Canada. Check the contract and your province’s or territory’s law before you sign.

sections.title: Quick Check: Choose the Best Next Move

items.title: How much more interest does the 84-month loan cost?
What happens when $4,000 of negative equity is rolled forward?
items.detail: It becomes extra principal in the new loan. That raises the amount financed, and usually the interest and the risk of being underwater.

items.title: Which document shows the total cost of borrowing?
items.detail: The disclosure statement, which you should get before the agreement is final.

items.title: How can you limit the effect on your score while comparing quotes?
items.detail: Get lender quotes within one focused two-week period. FCAC says the bureaus treat car-loan quotes in that period as one inquiry.

items.title: What should you check before you assume you can cancel?
items.detail: The signed contract and your province’s or territory’s dealer and consumer law. There is no national next-day cancellation right.

blocks.text: FCAC: Protection when buying a car
Use one sheet per offer, with the same assumptions each time. Leave out full account numbers and your driver’s licence number.
A complete sheet gives you what a weekly payment cannot: a reasoned yes, a reasoned no or a precise counteroffer.

items.title: Amount financed
items.text: The amount you borrow after the down payment, trade, fees, taxes, add-ons and rolled-in debt are counted.

items.title: APR
items.text: Annual percentage rate. The yearly cost of credit, used to compare loan offers.

items.title: Negative equity
items.text: The amount by which your vehicle loan balance is more than the vehicle is worth.

items.title: Loan term
items.text: The period over which you make your scheduled payments.

items.title: Lien
items.text: A lender’s registered claim against the vehicle until the loan is paid off.

items.title: Disclosure statement
items.text: The document before the contract that explains the cost of borrowing and the key credit terms.
